intent.quote: I guess my intent is that the agent and plumb is the interface for the User to interact with the system. So the agent should have the required tools to present context as best as possible.
intent.readback: You work with the system you are building through the agent and plumb, in your own words. You never type a shell command, never need plumb's inner workings, and never name a record by its number: no command of yours takes an id, and there is no approval command. You are never asked to read what the AI wrote in order to approve it; you only answer questions, through the question tool or the browser study room.
will: Every plumb capability you act on or need to see is reached through /plumb in plain words, your message read by meaning, or a question put to you through the question tool or the browser study room.
Everything you read names things by their title and your own words, explains any idea it needs first in one plain sentence, and names no shell command, record number, file or test name.
plumb's internal mechanisms (linking, repinning, hashing, test selection, log upkeep) are run by plumb and the agent, never asked of you.
The Obsidian vault stays a generated view you can open on request; editing it changes nothing.
wont: Any owner command that takes a record id, including /plumb approve <ids> or /plumb confirm <ids>.
Read-back or choice cards you read and press to approve what the AI wrote.
Asking you to run, or know of, plumb's shell commands or internal mechanisms.
An owner-only switch (such as automatic approval) turned on by the agent without your words.
assumptions: The agent itself may still call plumb's CLI with ids; only what reaches you is free of them.
explain (alias why), status, review, impact, view and init stay as plain-word /plumb verbs; approve and confirm leave the owner's command.
Saying in conversation that a record is wrong is how you reverse a judge-approved record (P3); plumb reads it as an answer, not a command.
A file or feature name you type yourself is accepted as plain words; plumb never requires one.

requirements.title: The owner reaches every plumb capability in plain words, never an id or a shell command
requirements.statement: Every capability the owner acts on or needs to see is reached through /plumb (also /plumb:plumb) with plain words, the owner's message read by meaning, or the question tool and browser study room. No owner command takes a record id and there is no approval command. Every verb the installed command advertises runs. Internal mechanisms (linking, repinning, hashing, test selection, log upkeep) stay internal, and an owner-only switch the agent starts on its own is refused.

examples.given: the plugin is installed in a repository
examples.then: plumb-records and plumb-clarify appear and /plumb:plumb runs the /plumb command (the host registers the plugin command under that name)

examples.given: the owner types /plumb:plumb intent the reminders should go by email
examples.then: it behaves exactly as /plumb intent the reminders should go by email

examples.given: the owner types /plumbing intent something
examples.then: it is not taken as a plumb command: no loop opens and nothing is released

examples.given: the session start says to type /plumb init to adopt this repository
examples.then: the agent runs plumb's adoption and reports what happened in the owner's terms

examples.given: no owner message asked for it
examples.when: the agent tries to turn automatic approval on
examples.then: it is refused and nothing changes

examples.given: two requirements about reminder timing
examples.when: the owner writes "the reminder timing looks right" in plain words
examples.then: the message is taken as the owner's answer about reminder timing, no record id or record text is shown to the owner, and no word list decided it

examples.given: the owner types "/plumb confirm the reminder timing" or "/plumb approve DEC-017"
examples.then: no approval command runs, no id is asked for, the records' states are unchanged by the command, and the words are taken as the owner's answer about reminder timing

examples.given: the list of plumb's capabilities, split into what the owner acts on and plumb's internal mechanisms
examples.then: every owner action is listed with its plain-words way to reach it, none takes an id, and no internal mechanism appears in the table, in owner-facing text or as a step the owner is asked to take

examples.given: a stale link that only needs repinning because its target was reformatted
examples.then: plumb or the agent repins it without telling the owner

examples.given: the installed /plumb command file
examples.when: each verb it advertises is run with --help
examples.then: each exits 0, and no verb is advertised that does not exist

examples_dropped.why: the automatic-approval switch is P9's, reached by the owner's words; its refusal side stays as SR-088/EX-2
P2 sharpened: no approval command and no owner command takes an id (/plumb approve DEC-017); the words are now read as an answer (SR-088/EX-10 reworded)
P2 sharpened: no /plumb confirm <id>, so no glance entry for one
the clarify --wait loop is agent mechanics under P6's intent loop, not the owner surface
the host API answering like the CLI is P14's thin-adapter behaviour, not an owner behaviour

proof.plan: Recommended: in a live Claude Code session the agent walks the owner-entry-point table; for each owner capability the owner types /plumb (once as /plumb:plumb) with plain words and sees it answered with no id asked for, and /plumb approve with an id is shown read as an answer rather than run. The owner decides whether this live walk or a recorded transcript of it is the proof.

requirements.title: plumb explain answers in plain words about a feature, a behaviour or a file
requirements.statement: /plumb explain (alias why) takes plain words or a repository path, never an id: words resolve to the best-matching records, a path to the requirements that own it. It answers with each record's title, state, the owner's quote, its examples and their test state, in the owner's terms; when two records match equally it describes both and picks neither; a file no requirement owns is said to be uncovered. The command's argument hint offers plain words.

examples.given: any build
examples.when: the owner asks /plumb why the invoices are rounded
examples.then: it gives the same answer as /plumb explain the invoices are rounded

examples.given: a requirement titled "Invoice totals are rounded to the cent"
examples.when: the owner asks /plumb explain how are invoice totals rounded?
examples.then: it answers with that requirement's title, state, the owner's quote, its examples and their test state, not a neighbouring requirement

examples.given: two requirements match "the export" equally
examples.when: the owner asks about the export
examples.then: both are described by title in the owner's terms and plumb picks neither

examples.given: billing.py is owned by a requirement and orphan.py by none
examples.when: the owner asks /plumb explain billing.py, then /plumb explain orphan.py
examples.then: the first answers with the owning requirement by title; the second says no requirement covers that file yet

examples.given: plumb is installed for Claude Code
examples.when: the /plumb command's argument hint is read
examples.then: it offers plain words ("explain <a feature, a behaviour or a file>"), never "<ID>"

examples_dropped.why: keyed on a record id (explain SR-001); the plain-words form SR-033/EX-3 carries the behaviour

proof.plan: Recommended: in a live Claude Code session the owner asks /plumb explain about a behaviour in their own words, about a file, and about a word two requirements share; each answer names the requirements by title, and the shared word gets both described with none chosen. The owner decides whether this is the proof.

requirements.title: Everything the owner reads speaks at the owner's level
requirements.statement: No text the owner sees (status, turn-end line, questions, /plumb answers, errors, merge and push reports, the study room, the vault) names a shell command, a record number without its title, a file or test name or an internal code; it names things by title and the owner's words and explains any needed idea first in one plain sentence. Owner quotes stay verbatim. Records the agent writes are checked and reworded before the owner sees them.

examples.given: a push carrying a requirement not yet approved
examples.then: it names the requirement by its title, says plumb will ask through the question tool if anything needs the owner's arbitration, and names no command to run, no way to skip the check and no record number

examples.given: a merge where code tied to a requirement changed
examples.then: it names that requirement by its title, any question for the owner comes through the question tool, and it names no command to run

examples.given: a turn that touched a decision
examples.then: it names the decision by its question in plain words, never by its number alone

examples.given: the owner asks why a merge is held, and the answer needs the idea that plumb remembers the exact wording approved
examples.then: the answer first says in one plain sentence that plumb remembers the exact wording approved and checks again when it changes, then uses it

examples.given: the README
examples.when: both checks (shell commands, inner workings) run on its owner sections
examples.then: they find nothing, and the agent's command reference sits in its own section

examples.given: the agent writes a requirement whose statement uses one of plumb's internal terms
examples.then: plumb refuses it and tells the agent which words to put in the owner's terms; the owner is asked nothing

examples.given: a record quotes the owner's own words, and those words mention a command
examples.then: the owner's words are kept exactly as the owner said them

examples.given: the owner asks what drifted, asks to see a requirement in full, or asks whether a requirement does what they meant
examples.then: it names each requirement by its title and its examples in plain words, says what to do next in plain words or a /plumb command without an id, and shows no record number, fingerprint, folder or file name or command to run unless the owner asks for detail

examples.given: one record approved by the judge and one by the owner's own answer
examples.then: it says "approved by the judge" or "approved by you", never a bare "approved"

examples.given: the owner's Windows console, where piped output is cp1252
examples.when: the agent shows any plumb answer with glyphs
examples.then: the glyphs print as UTF-8 and the answer never fails on encoding

proof.plan: Recommended: the two owner-text checks (shell commands, inner workings) run over every owner surface and pass; then in a live session the owner sees a held merge report, a turn-end line and a /plumb explain answer, each naming things by title with no command, id or file name. The owner decides which of these is the proof.

requirements.title: The Obsidian view is generated and never approves
requirements.statement: On the owner's request plumb writes an Obsidian vault, one note per record with links by title, plus an intent-map canvas, generated and byte-identical on regeneration. plumb never reads the vault back, so editing a note changes no record. A note names no command to run and no record id.

examples.given: a repository with records
examples.then: the two outputs are byte-identical

examples.given: the owner edits a requirement's note in the vault to say approved
examples.then: the requirement's state is unchanged

examples.given: the generated intent-map canvas
examples.then: it is valid JSON Canvas with unique node ids and an edge for each derives-from link

examples.given: a requirement awaits arbitration
examples.when: the owner opens its note in the vault
examples.then: the note says plumb will ask in the session through the question tool, names no command to run and no id, and shows its links by title

proof.plan: Recommended: the owner asks /plumb view, opens the vault in Obsidian, sees the intent map and a note, edits the note, and sees plumb's status unchanged. The owner decides whether that is the proof.

retired_decisions.why: the names of plumb's shell commands (validate, tests map, hooks install, statusline) are internal under P2: the owner never types them, so their naming is no longer the owner's decision
